hooks.text: A cosmic signal reached Earth fainter than a lunar cell phone.
What cosmic flash reaches Earth fainter than a cell phone on the Moon?
A millisecond deep-space flash can outshine our Sun for days.

title: The Cosmic Signal Stronger Than the Sun
description: Fast radio bursts are millisecond-long flashes of energy from deep space. Though they arrive incredibly weak, their true cosmic power is staggering.

beats.text: A cosmic signal reached Earth fainter than a lunar cell phone.
beats.visual: artist's concept of a weak radio signal arriving at Earth from deep space

beats.text: In 2007, astrophysicist Duncan Lorimer discovered this weak whisper in archival data from 2001.
beats.visual: photograph of the Parkes Observatory Radio Telescope in Australia

beats.text: The signal, a fast radio burst, traveled billions of light-years from outside our galaxy.
beats.visual: Hubble Space Telescope image of the Small Magellanic Cloud galaxy

beats.text: Although the blast lasted only a few milliseconds, its physical scale is truly staggering.
beats.visual: illustration of a pulsar emitting intense radio beams into space

beats.text: In that single instant, it released more energy than our Sun radiates in several days.
beats.visual: extreme ultraviolet image of the Sun showing a massive solar flare

beats.text: Even wilder, researchers recently detected repeating bursts that last just millionths of a second.
beats.visual: artist's concept of a highly magnetic magnetar emitting bursts

beats.text: Astronomers estimate that up to ten thousand of these titanic blasts occur every single day.
beats.visual: photograph of the Canadian Hydrogen Intensity Mapping Experiment radio telescope array

beats.text: They bombard our planet constantly, arriving almost completely silent.
beats.visual: photograph of the Arecibo Observatory radio telescope dish in Puerto Rico

better_than_last: Replaced historical discovery dates with immediate physical scale comparisons in early beats to maintain pacing and momentum after the hook.
